speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a significant medical history; could you please tell me which conditions you have been diagnosed with previously? Additionally, when did you first notice the gait and limb ataxia?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. To narrow this down, have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as blurred or double vision, or any trouble with your speech? Also, does this clumsiness improve when you sleep and worsen in the morning?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, the sudden onset of ataxia and "drunken" gait strongly suggests JC virus reactivation. I am requesting an MRI of the brain to confirm the diagnosis and request results of a plasma JC virus antibody test.
